title: Introduce epochal drift decoupler and traffic contrast guard
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add epochal drift decoupler to distinguish long-term traffic/model shifts from transient regressions; add traffic contrast guard to enable cohort-aware rollback gating. Backwards compatible, feature-flagged rollout.
description: Motivation: Continuous canary detectors at Redwood have been sensitive to epochal shifts in traffic composition (e.g., sudden customer cutover, model mix change) which produce wide-area baseline drift and cause noisy, high false-positive rollbacks. This PR introduces two complementary components: 1) an epochal drift decoupler that identifies baseline shifts that persist beyond short windows and adjusts the baseline used by downstream detectors; 2) a traffic contrast guard that computes cohort-level contrasts (internal vs external customers, sampled vs full traffic, model-variant groups) and only escalates when a regression manifests consistently across contrasted cohorts. Design summary: The epochal decoupler observes metric trajectories at multiple horizons and fits a lightweight epoch model (piecewise constant + low-degree trend) to detect sustained baseline changes. When an epoch boundary is detected, the decoupler emits an annotated baseline event and isolates short-term residuals for canary evaluators. The traffic contrast guard runs pairwise cohort comparisons with robust quantile summaries and uses a consensus rule (majority of cohorts + min-effect-size threshold) to suppress rollouts driven by composition change. Config knobs: epoch_window_ms, min_epoch_duration_secs, contrast_min_cohorts, min_effect_qdelta, sensitivity_beta. Feature flag: perf.epochal_decoupler.enabled (off by default). Testing: unit tests for epoch segmentation, synthetic scenario harness in perf-canary/e2e that simulates customer cutover and model swap effects, and replay tests against last 30 days of canary history to validate false positive rate reduction. Rollout plan: enable in staging for 48h, shadow mode in prod for 7 days (no rollbacks), opt-in canary routes at 10% traffic, then enable gating on low-risk clusters before global switch. Observability: new metrics perf.epochal_decoupler.epoch_count, perf.epochal_decoupler.boundary_latency, perf.traffic_contrast.guard_decisions with tags for cohorts and decisions. Dashboards: canary-epoch-overview, traffic-contrast-matrix. Backwards compatibility: downstream detectors operate unchanged unless they read the annotated baseline event; fallback: when feature-flag off or decoupler errors, system falls back to current baseline logic. Related: ENG-18234 (false-positive canary reduction), ENG-19002 (cohort-based gating). This change is primarily algorithmic + small API surface for canary config. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] e2e replay, [x] docs + runbook, [x] monitoring + alerts.
